description: Reduce launch/sync overhead and exploit libraries on the small/mid shapes (n=176 shape1 278us, n=352 shape2 737us, B=40). Profile shows many tiny serial panel/larft/lacpy launches. Try a CUTLASS/cuBLASLt batched-GEMM-backed blocked QR or a single fused megakernel that does panel+trailing for the whole B=40 batch with one launch per block-column, minimizing host-device syncs and kernel-launch count. Compare against a cuSOLVER batched geqrf (gels/geqrfBatched) baseline to see if a library call wins outright at these sizes.

n=352 bf16 single-level: fold build_V into the cmf panel write-back. The FP32 n=176 path already folds V (passes Vp to the panel, skips build_V_kernel), but the bf16 n=352 single-level path launched a standalone build_V_kernel<bf16> per outer block (~6 launches, grid=40 latency-bound). Pass Vp to the cmf panel (it builds the m_o x ob packed bf16 V in its write-back, byte-identical layout) and skip build_V. Gated to single-level cmf-eligible blocks (defer==5, g_panel_cm2, no OV fold, m_o<=352). WIN: shape2 737.5->721.2us (-2.2%), geomean 2085.3->2079.3 (-0.29%). 22/22 validate PASS. shape1 unchanged (already folded).

Brief-0 (n=176/352, B=40) DONE. WIN committed (9588415b): fold build_V into the n=352 bf16 single-level cmf panel write-back, dropping the standalone build_V_kernel<bf16> launches (the FP32 n=176 path already folded; bf16 didn't). shape2 737.5->720.9us (-2.2%), geomean 2085.3->2078.8 (-0.3%), 22/22 validate. Isolated profiling (NOT whole-bench, which is checker-contaminated) shows the REAL bottleneck for both shapes is the per-matrix wsp_cmf PANEL kernel (n=176 71%, n=352 70%), latency-bound at grid=40 (ncu: waves=0.27, 73% theoretical speedup if SMs filled, 13.7% compute/12.9% mem), with build_Minv #2 (15-18%, also grid-40). The brief's premises were wrong here: trailing GEMMs are already tensor-core (s1688/nvjet), not SIMT. WHAT LOSES (measured): cuSOLVER torch.geqrf is 70x SLOWER (20037us n=176!); CholeskyQR fails PD in FP32 even with column equilibration (cond=1 still squares cond past FP32), and FP64-Gram CholeskyQR is 456us>283us; batched trsm for build_Minv (33-41us) > current per-CTA build_Minv+matmul (~30us); cm_coop pivot-coop REGRESSES (737->895us, tuned for n=2048); pure-FP16 fails orth gate at n=352 (5.35e-3>4.2e-3). block/warps/minv_blk4/minv_nt all already at optimum (swept). Multi-CTA m-split + multi-step cm2 panels were build-light-pruned by prior workers (don't win at B=40). A fused panel+trailing megakernel is COUNTERPRODUCTIVE at B=40 (would force the device-filling batched trailing GEMMs to grid-40). SUGGESTED NEXT: these shapes are at a hard local optimum bounded by the B=40 occupancy floor (40 CTAs/148 SMs) on a latency-bound serial-Householder panel; remaining headroom is small. If pursuing, the only untested lever is reviving a TARGETED multi-CTA m-split JUST for the first large-m panels (m=352/288), but prior abandonment suggests low odds. Leaderboard: we are RANK 3 (2078us), gap to #1 (nikhilbarhate99, 1983us) ~4.8% -- frontier is micro-opt; the small shapes' geomean leverage is real so this -0.3% helps.

This hides every per-step launch/latency gap on one stream behind the other matrix's work. recon_lu 7063->5477us microbench (-22%), Hdev~4e-10 vs sequential (numerically identical). Also added a dynamic-smem diag_lu variant for w>64 (block-width sweep showed bs=64 still optimal, so it stays at 64, but the kernel is in place). shape6 13592->13065us, geomean 2072.658->2065.041 (-0.69% vs baseline 2079.314). 19/19 validate PASS.

(4) Dpotrf 2-stream: no help, the n=4096 FP64 chol already saturates the device. (5) main-solve TRSM nb 384->512: -76us BUT broke the orth gate (residual 0.0536>0.0488 at the bench seed; the ||QtQ-I||_max microprobe didn't predict it) -- nb stays 384.
